newsitem.title: USA: Republicans end budget talks, to meet White House.
newsitem.headline: Republicans end budget talks, to meet White House.

text.p: House and Senate Republicans wrapped up internal negotiations on spending and tax provisions for balanced budget legislation and prepared to open talks with the administration later Wednesday.
Republicans did not reach agreement on several key issues, including whether to support a 20 cents per pack cigarette tax increase approved by the Senate. The House has major concerns about the plan.
"We don't have to (decide) right now and my position certainly is the House has got real heartburn over a cigarette tax," said Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer.
Archer said he did not consider tobacco taxes to be a litmus test for the administration, in terms of whether they could support a final tax bill.

Republicans also did not reach unified positions on certain spending issues, including cuts in Medicaid payments to hospitals that serve a large number of poor people. They decided to provide at least $16 billion for a new children's health initiative.
Final funding depends on the fate of the tobacco tax. The Senate had allocated $8 billion in tax revenues for children's health care.
